NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via pH and conductivity measurements to detect scaling conditions.  
Departure: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) at pump impeller surfaces to directly measure silica adsorption kinetics, bypassing bulk property inference.  
Connection: Silica scaling initiates at interfaces via adsorption; EIS detects interfacial charge transfer changes proportional to surface coverage.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Double-layer capacitance (C_dl) ∝ 1/adsorbed_layer_thickness.  
Magnitude: Silica monolayer (~0.5 nm) reduces C_dl by ~20% (verified via Stern model for 0.1M SiO₂ at 25°C).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Instrument: Impedance analyzer (ALREADY-RECORDED: "pump vibration sensors" repurposed for EIS probes).  
- Probe: Titanium electrodes (ALREADY-RECORDED: "existing pump material specs").  
- Input stream: Impedance magnitude at 1 kHz (ALREADY-RECORDED: "pump electrical telemetry").  
- Threshold: ΔC_dl > 15% (CALCULATED: from Stern model for 0.1M SiO₂ at 25°C).  
- Procedure: Weekly 5-min EIS scan during pump operation (ALREADY-RECORDED: "routine maintenance schedule").  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)

- Operability: SAME (no operator intervention; automated scan triggers).  
- Maintenance: SAME (probe lifespan matches pump overhaul interval).

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: EIS scan during silica saturation test (stated: "lab-scale silica scaling trials").  
Instruments: Impedance analyzer, temperature probe.  
Pass/fail: ΔC_dl > 15% within 24h of saturation.  
Duration: 48h trial.  
Kill criterion: No impedance change after saturation.  
Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED "silica concentration vs. time" data.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: ΔC_dl (directly measures adsorption kinetics).  
Secondary supplement: pH (confirms bulk chemistry).  
Rationale: The problem states "choking flow" as failure, driven by interfacial adsorption, making EIS the primary mechanism.
